system.label: Agent identity and rules
system.text:
You are a senior software engineer on a team that maintains a production Python codebase. You
have been handed one change request. You own it from understanding the requirement to delivering
code that a reviewer can approve and merge.

Your responsibilities

Understand the requirement.
- Read the request as the product team means it, not only its literal words. Work out the inputs,
  the expected outputs, the error cases and the edge cases it implies.
- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the
  system and with what users of the feature would expect.

Understand the code before changing it.
- Read the code you are changing and the code it depends on or that depends on it, as far as it is
  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given
- <task>: the change request from the product team.
- <context>: material from the repository. How much varies: it may be a single file or much of the
  project. It is what you know about the codebase.

What you can and cannot do
- You cannot run code, and there is no one to ask.
- If tools are provided with this request, you may use them to look at the repository before you
  answer. If no tools are provided, you cannot open files or search: deliver the finished change in
  this reply. Tool calls, plans and requests for more files written as text are not executed, and a
  reply without code counts as no change.
- If something you need is not shown, make the most reasonable assumption consistent with what is
  shown, and implement it.

Output format (strict)
Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or
modify, each wrapped exactly as:
<file path="PATH">
...full file contents...
</file>
- Replace PATH with the file's real path relative to the repository root, as shown in <context> or
  <task>.
- Always the whole file, never a diff or an excerpt, and no placeholders such as "rest unchanged".
- Files you don't change are left out.
- Return nothing outside the <file> blocks: no explanations, plans or summaries before or after them.

user.label: Task (change request)
user.text:
Customers can now leave a delivery note for the courier (for example "leave it with the neighbour
at no. 5"). Add `delivery_note: str = ""` to orders and make it work end to end: a new database
migration adds a `delivery_note` column to the orders table (text, empty by default); the order
repository saves the note when an order is added and loads it back; the order page shows it under a
"Delivery note" heading, only when there is one; and the order JSON in the API includes it as
`delivery_note`. Notes are at most 200 characters: storing a longer one raises ValueError.

    return _Seller(*a, **kw)
from shopkit.pricing.currency import Rate, RateTable

START, END = date(2026, 3, 2), date(2026, 3, 8)
OLD = date(2026, 1, 15)          # delivered long ago: outside the return window


def _batch(sellers, earnings, adjustments=(), rollover=None, holds=None, **kw):
    return build_payout_batch(sellers, list(earnings), list(adjustments), START, END, holds=holds or HoldBook(),
                              rollover=rollover or Rollover(), **kw)


def test_commission_refunds_and_net():
    s = Seller("S1", "Pots & Co")
    res = _batch([s], [Earning("S1", "O1", "POT", 10_000, OLD), Earning("S1", "O2", "PAN", 5_000, OLD, refunded_cents=1_000)])
    p = res.payouts[0]
    assert p.commission_cents == 2_250 and p.net_cents == 10_000 - 1_500 + 5_000 - 750 - 1_000 and p.status == DRAFT


def test_full_refund_returns_commission():
    res = _batch([Seller("S1", "x")], [Earning("S1", "O1", "POT", 10_000, OLD, refunded_cents=10_000),
                                       Earning("S1", "O2", "POT", 10_000, OLD)])
    assert res.payouts[0].lines[0].net_cents == 0 and res.payouts[0].lines[0].commission_cents == 0


def test_recent_deliveries_are_held_and_released_later():
    holds = HoldBook()
    s = Seller("S1", "x")
    res = _batch([s], [Earning("S1", "O1", "POT", 10_000, date(2026, 3, 5))], holds=holds)
    assert res.payouts[0].held_cents == 8_500 and res.payouts[0].status == ROLLED_OVER     # nothing left to pay
    later = build_payout_batch([s], [], [], date(2026, 4, 6), date(2026, 4, 12), holds=holds, rollover=Rollover())
    assert later.payouts[0].adjustments_cents == 8_500


def test_small_payouts_roll_over_unless_the_seller_is_closing():
    rollover = Rollover()
    tiny = [Earning("S1", "O1", "PIN", 2_000, OLD), Earning("S2", "O2", "PIN", 2_000, OLD)]
    res = _batch([Seller("S1", "x"), Seller("S2", "y", status=CLOSING)], tiny, rollover=rollover)
    by = {p.seller_id: p for p in res.payouts}
    assert by["S1"].status == ROLLED_OVER and rollover.balances == {"S1": 1_700}
    assert by["S2"].status == DRAFT and by["S2"].net_cents == 1_700 < MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS
    nxt = _batch([Seller("S1", "x")], [Earning("S1", "O3", "PIN", 2_000, OLD)], rollover=rollover)
    assert nxt.payouts[0].carried_in_cents == 1_700 and nxt.payouts[0].status == DRAFT


def test_negative_balances_carry_forward_even_when_closing():
    rollover = Rollover()
    res = _batch([Seller("S1", "x", status=CLOSING)], [], [Adjustment("S1", -3_000, "chargeback", "CB1")], rollover=rollover)
    assert res.payouts[0].status == ROLLED_OVER and rollover.balances == {"S1": -3_000}


def test_suspended_sellers_skipped_and_bad_earnings_rejected():
    res = _batch([Seller("S1", "x", status=SUSPENDED), Seller("S2", "y")],
                 [Earning("S1", "O1", "A", 100_000, OLD), Earning("S2", "O2", "A", 5_000, OLD, refunded_cents=6_000)])
    assert res.skipped == {"S1": "suspended"} and res.stats["earnings_valid"] == 1


def test_reserve_and_currency_conversion():
    rates = RateTable()
    rates.add(Rate("USD", "EUR", END, 900_000))
    s = Seller("S1", "x", payout_currency="EUR", reserve_bp=1000)
    res = _batch([s], [Earning("S1", "O1", "A", 100_000, OLD)], rates=rates)
    p = res.payouts[0]
    assert p.reserve_cents == 10_000
    # net 75_000 USD -> 67_500 EUR - 1.5% fee (1_013) = 66_487
    assert p.net_cents == 66_487 and any("fee 1013" in n for n in p.notes)
    assert "S1" in _batch([s], [Earning("S1", "O1", "A", 100_000, OLD)]).skipped


def test_trace_flag_and_statement():
    s = Seller("S1", "Pots & Co")

    p = res.payouts[0]
    approve(p, "fin")
    text = statement_text(p, s)

                                                           Earning("S2", "O2", "A", 10_000, OLD)],

    by = {p.seller_id: p for p in res.payouts}
    assert by["S1"].net_cents == 8_500 - 2_040 and by["S2"].net_cents == 8_500


def test_already_paid_and_duplicate_lines_are_skipped():
    metrics = {}
    e = Earning("S1", "O1", "A", 10_000, OLD)
    res = _batch([Seller("S1", "x")], [e, e, Earning("S1", "O2", "A", 10_000, OLD)],
                 paid_lines={("S1", "O2", "A")}, metrics=metrics)
    assert len(res.payouts[0].lines) == 1 and metrics["payouts.dup_in_batch"] == 1
    assert metrics["payouts.dup_already_paid"] == 1 and metrics["payouts.drafts"] == 1
    dry = _batch([Seller("S1", "x")], [e, e], settings=Settings(feature_flags={"payout_dedupe_dry_run": True}))
